name: Darbhanga
why_it_matters: The fine-dining room of BrijRama Palace, an 18th-century haveli on Darbhanga Ghat. Strictly pure-veg with no alcohol — bylaw-compliant for the ghat zone. The terrace Udayan and the riverboat dining option are bookable separately.
insider_tip: Reach by boat from Dashashwamedh — the lane approach is steep and unmarked. Book riverboat dining at least 24 hours ahead; the in-restaurant terrace is easier same-day.
signature_address: BrijRama Palace, Darbhanga Ghat, Munshi Ghat Road, Varanasi 221001

name: Keshav Tambul Bhandar
why_it_matters: The Banarasi paan counter near Ravidas Gate, Lanka — the spot that serves the prime minister when he's in his constituency. Magai leaf, gulkand, supari and chuna assembled in 60 seconds; eat standing.
insider_tip: Ask for meetha (sweet) if you don't chew tobacco — the saada and benarasi versions contain stronger fillings. They allow watching the assembly process if you ask politely.
signature_address: Swastik Plaza, near Ravidas Gate, Lanka, Varanasi 221005

name: Baati Chokha Restaurant
why_it_matters: First fine-dining chain in India built around baati-chokha — the roasted wheat ball with mashed-brinjal-tomato chokha that's eastern UP's defining village meal. Mud-house ambience, sal-leaf plates by default.
insider_tip: Order baati with desi ghee on the side — the menu version is plain unless you ask. If you've never had chokha, the brinjal version is the canonical entry; tomato chokha is hotter.
signature_address: Behind Anand Mandir Cinema Hall, Raja Bazaar Road, Teliyabagh, Varanasi 221002
